prognosis.source_quote: Dilatations smaller than 4 cm are generally considered low-risk for rupture. They can be monitored annually without immediate intervention. Dilatations over 4 cm require close monitoring and, in certain cases, intervention to prevent complications such as dissection or rupture. The prognosis is worse if the dilatation is over 4.5 cm [1, 2, 3]. Hereditary aortic disease is associated with greater risk including rate of progression.

summary.source_quote: Aortic dilatation refers to the abnormal enlargement of the aorta, the largest blood vessel in the body. Aortic dissection is a serious condition where a tear occurs in the inner layer of the aorta.
summary.value: Aortic dilatation refers to the abnormal enlargement of the aorta, the largest blood vessel in the body. Aortic dissection is a serious condition where a tear occurs in the inner layer of the aorta.

symptoms.source_quote: Symptoms may include back pain, cough, shortness of breath, chest pain. However, most cases are asymptomatic until dissection occurs.

treatment.source_quote: Medication: beta blockers, angiotensin receptor blockers, statins. Surgery and/or procedures: open chest surgery, aortic root surgery, valve aortic root repair
